Definition: from G4862 and G482; to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist):--help.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the Spirit helps our infirmities, for we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the Spirit makes intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Martha says the same word to Jesus in the kitchen: bid my sister help me, for I am left to serve alone. The Spirit takes hold with us in prayer the way a friend takes hold of the other end of a burden.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the Spirit takes hold with me when I do not know how to pray, and I believe His groanings carry what my words cannot.
